articles.title: Maia Bouchier powers England to record ODI run chase against Ireland
articles.summary: Ireland: 281-5; England: 283-4. Bouchier hits 104; three 50s by Ireland batters. A century from Maia Bouchier led England to a record one-day international run chase against Ireland at Leicester on Tuesday, as they reached their target of 282 with six wickets and 71 balls to spare.
body: Bouchier missed out on selection for the T20 World Cup in June but remains a key part of England’s ODI plans, as they look to build a new team in the wake of the retirements of Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont.

Here, Bouchier initially played second fiddle to Sophia Dunkley, who smashed a ferocious 73 from 61 balls. But when Dunkley sent a return catch into the hands of the leg-spinner Cara Murray, it was left to Bouchier to bring up the three-figure score which was there for the taking against a helpless-looking Irish attack.

England are contesting these three ODIs without several key players – Nat Sciver-Brunt remains injured, while Lauren Bell, Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Sophie Ecclestone, Amy Jones and Linsey Smith are being rested. The series therefore provides an intriguing glimpse into the future, with the 21-year-old Jodi Grewcock batting at No 3, and the off-spinning all-rounder Mady Villiers also making a white-ball return after two years in the wilderness.

articles.title: Superb England crush Ireland with record ODI chase
articles.summary: Maia Bouchier's stunning century helps England women seal their record one-day international chase of 282 to beat Ireland in the series opener.
body: England's new era started with a dominant six-wicket win over Ireland as they cruised to their record chase of 282 in the first one-day international.
Opener Maia Bouchier struck a stunning 104 off 95 balls to secure England's highest chase in women's ODIs with 11.5 overs to spare.
Bouchier added 143 for the first wicket with Sophia Dunkley, who made 73, which laid the perfect platform before the centurion holed out to long-on with just 59 runs needed.

Alice Capsey and Freya Kemp made light work of those remaining runs with a quickfire stand of 54 off 38 balls to put England within touching distance, Capsey hitting the winning boundary to finish unbeaten on 41.

articles.title: Taylor prepared for test rather than testimonial
articles.summary: Katie Taylor is preparing for a stern test from Flora Pili rather than a Croke Park testimonial on Saturday night as she seeks to sign off on her career in style.
body: Over 54 years will have passed since Muhammad Ali headlined the last boxing event at the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association.
Just as 'The Greatest' blazed a trail in a career that transcended sport, Taylor has done likewise.

Elevating women's boxing to heights never experienced or perhaps expected, the 40-year-old will make her final walk in front of 80,000 fans with the opportunity to become undisputed champion at light-welterweight once again.

It is all set up for the glorious farewell, and while talk about ring-walks and musical entertainment is a feature of fight week in Dublin, Taylor is looking no further than her 29-year-old French opponent, who is perfect through 12 fights and holds the European and IBO belt.

articles.title: A rodeo that started in Minnesota two years ago comes to Sam Houston Race Park in November
articles.summary: Instead of horses galloping around a race track, a professional rodeo will take over Sam Houston Race Park for two nights in November. Athletes with the largest professional rodeo organization - the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association - will compete on Nov.
body: The co-founders of the event first teamed up to host a rodeo at the Canterbury Park horse racing track outside Minneapolis, Minn., in 2024 and began envisioning a nationwide series earlier this year, according to their website. They started selling tickets for their stop in Houston last month.

"Sam Houston Race Park is an outstanding venue with a rich history, and we're excited to bring this experience to Texas while supporting the important work being done by Camp Hope," Kip Rakos, CEO and co-founder of Rodeo at the Racetrack, said in a July statement. "Our goal is to create an unforgettable weekend for fans while making a meaningful impact in the community."
Rakos said he will continue to expand the event through Texas with similar rodeos at Lone Star Park in Dallas and Retama Park in San Antonio next year.

articles.title: Angels Sold to Rams Owner, Creating New Top Owner in LA Sports
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Angels are being sold to the owner of another LA franchise, bringing to an end a season of tumult for one of the worst teams in baseball and further solidifying the sports empire of Stan Kroenke and his company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment.
body: Arte Moreno, who has owned the Angels since 2023, is dealing the team to Kroenke, owner of the LA Rams, reports Nate Atkins, Rams reporter for The Athletic.
Moreno has been the subject of protests from Angels fans who bemoaned the last-place team, including chants from fans and even aerial messages.

Despite fielding teams including superstars Mike Trout and Shohei Ohtani, the Angels have repeatedly failed to make an impact in MLB, even to the point that Trout has played in only three playoff games for the entirely of his 16-year career, all of which came in 2014.

“The Moreno Family has been honored to steward the Angels for 23 years and we believe with KSE’s experience and success they are the best next owner for the franchise,” Moreno said in a news release announcing the sale. “The Angels Organization looks forward to continuing its commitment to the fans, our employees, the players and our business partners.”

articles.title: Experimental England storm to highest ODI chase in win over Ireland
articles.summary: England breezed to their highest successful ODI chase after an iffy fielding and bowling performance as an experimental side beat Ireland by six wickets in the series opener at Leicester.
body: Maia Bouchier (104 off 95 balls) and Sopha Dunkley (73 off 61) smoked 143 for the opening wicket inside 20 overs before Bouchier went on to notch her second ODI century as England reached their target of 282 with 71 deliveries to spare.

Freya Kemp (36 off 22) drilled four fours in a row off Arlene Kelly in the 34th over - a feat Bouchier had managed off Jane Maguire towards the start of the chase - as the all-rounder dominated a 54-run partnership from 38 balls with Alice Capsey (41no off 40), after Capsey and Bouchier had combined to add 50 off 47.

England's previous record ODI run chase was the 267-8 they knocked off against Australia in Bristol during the home Ashes in 2023, a game in which Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont posted the two highest scores.

With Knight and Beaumont now retired and team stalwarts Nat Sciver-Brunt, Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Amy Jones rested for this three-match assignment, Dunkley and Bouchier played the key roles, albeit aided by some error-strewn stuff from Ireland.

articles.title: Everton Eye £40m Striker As Transfer Deadline Hits Final Hours: Right Choice For Moyes?
articles.summary: Everton have made a formal offer to sign Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s transfer deadline, according to journalist Sami Mobkel. The 25-year-old American forward, currently at AS Monaco, is valued at around £40m by the French club.
body: Everton are not alone in their interest. Tottenham ‘s Richarlison is also floating as a backup option, though the Brazilian is still considering his options and a deal looks far from done. With the window slamming shut in hours, Everton are pushing hard.

Balogun’s season at Monaco was, on paper, genuinely impressive. He scored 13 goals and added four assists across 30 Ligue 1 appearances last term, then chipped in with five goals in 10 Champions League outings. He carried that form into the 2026 FIFA World Cup, netting three times in four games for the United States, becoming the first American since 1930 to score a World Cup brace. Monaco want to cash in now. Everton are ready to spend. The question is whether the two clubs can actually agree on a price.

Everton’s initial valuation of Balogun sat somewhere between €18m and €20m, roughly £15m to £16.5m. Monaco want close to £40m. That is not a negotiation gap. That is a chasm. And while the prospective £60m sale of Iliman Ndiaye to Tottenham does open some financial headroom, committing £40m of that on a single forward represents a significant gamble for a club still operating under the Premier League’s cost-ratio regime.

articles.title: Dual Gold Cup winner Galopin Des Champs dies aged 10
articles.summary: Two-time Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Galopin Des Champs has died from injuries sustained in an accident in a field less than a week after being retired by connections.
body: The 2023 and 2024 winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup, Galopin Des Champs has tragically died following an accident in a field; The 10-year-old horse, who was trained by Willie Mullins, was found with a severe injury on his near front leg.
Ruby Walsh revealed the news late on Tuesday evening that the 10-year-old gelding had suffered an injury to his near front leg which vets concluded was irreparable.
"Sadly Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved," Walsh said in a statement to Racing TV.
"He was checked a few times throughout the morning but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg.
